about: Every version of the instructions a model is given in the pipeline, and its state (decisions 147.a, 148.a). A new version starts as a prototype: frozen and hashed beside the active one (frozen_contract.json holds its sha256), run only on chosen pages, its results kept apart and never served. It becomes active only by a person's decision after its gate, written before the run; the version it replaces is then retired, never deleted. One version per role is active. `parts` names what each file of a version is: the reader's rules, the reader's output format, the judge's instructions, the class check's.

parts.rules: Reader: what to transcribe and how faithfully, the blocks and their classes
parts.format: Format: the page file the reader writes, Markdown blocks with YAML front matter
parts.judge: Judge: how a model compares a reading with the page image, and what counts as a finding
parts.classcheck: Class check: a cheap model names which classes a page holds, before any reading is bought
parts.correction: Correction: a model proposes how one block should read, from the page image and a judge's finding, for a person to record or not

versions.title: Markdown blocks, contract page/1
versions.why: The mini pilot's choice: Markdown blocks, 20 of 20 valid and 112 of 112 formulas exact on 20 free pages (decision OC-1.a).

versions.title: page/1 + eight rules from the walk and judge/4
versions.why: page/1's rules unchanged, plus a section of eight: table grids with operator columns, T-accounts as tables, a table's printed title, legible images of tables read, chart values read against the axis, counts only as counted, a photo's own text left out, index numbers digit by digit. Each from a reader error a person confirmed in the walk of 10 Nov or a rule judge/4 proposed (decisions 197.a, 207.a). The contract stays page/1. Its gate: the mini pilot's 20 pages against publisher gold (nothing lost against page/1), and the walk's six reader errors checked by code (at least four fixed).

versions.title: page/1 + a backslash printed as text
versions.why: page/1's rules unchanged, plus one sentence beside the inline marks: a backslash the page prints as text is written \, inside math \backslash, the spelling validator page/1.4 accepts (F4.a, the operator, 18 Nov). page/1 named no way to write one, so every reader failed on such a page. The contract stays page/1. Its gate, written before the run: the mini pilot's 20 pages lose nothing against page/1 (all valid, formulas and table cells as exact against publisher gold), and the nine free pages whose readings failed only on a LaTeX command outside math all become valid (cells P3-MP-SM and P3-BS-SM).

versions.title: The judge as measured in the mini pilot
versions.why: Measured in the mini pilot: 48 of 49 planted errors caught, 0 of 8 clean pages flagged.

versions.title: judge/1 + proper names are not errors
versions.why: judge/1 called a proper name a wrong word although its own evidence said printed and written alike (free finance p. 5, 'Carlyse'); one sentence under NOT AN ERROR on proper names, brands and unusual spellings (decision 147.a). Its gate: at least 48 of 49 planted errors, 0 of 8 clean pages, and every page with a person's verdict.

versions.title: judge/2 + printed and written must differ
versions.why: judge/2 still called 'Carlyse' wrong when run live on finance p. 5 (9 Nov), quoting 'Carlyse Ciocca' and 'Carlyse', both as the reading writes them: the judge compares, finds the two alike and reports anyway. judge/2 plus one change in FINDINGS: a finding needs printed X and written Y different, and the judge reads the block again before it reports a word or a value. The same gate as judge/2.

versions.title: judge/2 on Opus 5.5, proposing rules for the reader
versions.why: Reader and judge were one model, so a blind spot they share went unseen (finance p. 94: both misread a chart's crossing). judge/2's instructions on another model, plus up to three rules per page for the reader: clear format rules, classes and attributes of the vocabulary, gathered and merged across pages (decisions 195.a, 197.a). Its gate: the planted errors and clean pages, and the 16 pages a person judged on 10 Nov.

versions.title: Which classes a page holds, named by a cheap model
versions.why: The second step of the cascade (decision 64.a): on every page the free rules call text only, it names the classes through a schema, never the text, for about 0.00026 USD a page; Haiku found structure on 28 of 200 licensed pages the rules had missed (14 %).

versions.title: A minimal correction of one block, the judge's finding a pointer
versions.why: The operator's W2.a (21 Nov): a person correcting a block from a judge's finding writes the block by hand; a model may propose it. It sees the page image, the block and every finding on it, takes the finding as a pointer to check in the image, never as a fact, and changes as little as it can. Its gate, written before the run: the person corrections whose block carries a finding the person rated right or right for a wrong reason (14 on 21 Nov, in both pipeline databases). Per case the person's edit and the proposal's edit, as words added and removed against the reading: a case passes with edit recall at least 0.8 and edit precision at least 0.6, or, for a description a person worded their own way, where line 1 reads that the proposal corrects every fact the person corrected and adds no error (listed by name). It passes with at least 11 of the 14, at least 2 of the 4 rated right for a wrong reason among them, so a judge's wrong evidence is not followed. The three false alarms and the one case without a rating are reported beside it. At most 0.60 USD. → now (run 21 Nov, 0.27 USD): failed, 8 of 14 (6 by words, 2 descriptions by line 1's reading: a swap of two values the word measure cannot see, and a fact worded otherwise), 1 of the rated right for a wrong reason, of which there are 3, not 4 as the gate said. The misses: three empty tables written as pipe tables, one with a header the page does not print (its own format line named |); a chart's crossing read as 2010 where the person read 2012; a value -9.5 where the person read -10; an unclear mark dropped where the person kept it.

versions.title: correction/1 + tables as HTML, inline marks kept, chart values at the axis
versions.why: correction/1's misses, each a rule: a table is HTML inside its block, never with a header the page does not print; the transcription's inline marks are kept, an unclear one too, the likelier reading first; a chart's value is read against the axis at the exact point, a crossing where the lines meet. Its gate, written before the run: the same 14 cases, 11 rated right and 3 right for a wrong reason; a case passes with edit recall at least 0.8 and edit precision at least 0.6, or, for a description or a swap of values the word measure cannot see, where line 1 reads that the proposal corrects every fact the person corrected and adds no error (listed by name). It passes with at least 11 of the 14 and 2 of the 3. At most 0.60 USD. → now (run 21 Nov, 0.27 USD): passed, 13 of 14 (11 by words, 2 descriptions by line 1's reading: a swap of two values, a fact worded otherwise), 2 of the 3; an unclear time cell came back exactly as the person wrote it. The miss: a chart's crossing the person read as 2012, the proposal as 2008 to 2010 (the judge's wrong 2006 to 2007 not followed). Beside the gate, on the three false alarms the proposal agreed with the judge at least in part each time, so a proposal never replaces a person's look at the image. → now, the same instructions on claude-opus-5-5 (the operator's A1.b, 21 Nov, 0.54 USD): 12 of 14, 2 of the 3. It read the chart's crossing as the person did (2012), which Sonnet, the reader's and the judge's model, missed; it kept the unclear time cell's first reading where the person put the other first (the word measure counts that a pass, being a swap; read, it is a miss), and read one chart value -9.5 where the person read -10. On the page without a finding it changed nothing and said so. → now, on 11 open issues without a person's verdict (the operator's C1.a, 21 Nov, 0.47 USD for both models), each proposal read by line 1 against the page image: Opus 9 of 11, Sonnet 6 of 11. The open issues held 4 false alarms of the judge (a chart value read right, an order's bars told from the volume's, an order count that is there, a formula that matches); Opus left all four as they were, Sonnet followed the judge on two and rewrote a third. Opus read an event graph's initializing arrows right where Sonnet did not. Both followed the judge on one chart value (0.35 read as 0.3) and missed the order of a blurred screenshot's axis labels.
